quote: I pretty rarely use AI in my typical workday. I tend to only use it when I need help coming up with new sales strategies or different ways to improve interactions with customers.
I will open the AI model and provide it with a scenario that I may run into at work and ask it to come up with a unique strategy to increase my chances of making a sale.
Do you typically use them as-is, or do you find yourself modifying them based on your own experience?
I always modify them. They're never "perfect". Sometimes they're repetitive or not relevant for my work. However, I still use the overall strategy.
I turn to AI when I'm stuck. For example, if there's a new product I'm selling and I don't know how to pitch it to someone, I will turn to AI for help.
I tend to give it all the context up front. I do not typically go back and forth with the AI.
One time I used AI to develop a strategy for selling a product I wasn't familiar with and it worked extremely well. I was very satisfied because I made the most sales that month out of my whole team.

I gave a lot of details in this specific scenario. I provided as much details as possible and I noticed it really made a difference. I also included information about myself and my personality to help the AI cater the strategy to myself as a person.
I think I will continue to use it the way I have. I hope in the future, the AI will improve and thus improve my performance at work as well.
No, that is all.
I use AI tools for brainstorming, asking quick questions about technique and theory, general admin, copywriting, emails/comms, and also business planning.
Oh I should mention I also use some machine learning mixing plugins like iZotope Ozone and Sonible Smart:EQ.
This wasn't a client project but I've been using AI to critically analyse film scores.
It was fun but also it helped me refine my own perspective somewhat. I was just sending through articles from the composer and suggesting other connections that might be considered.

I'm honestly doing a lot my "bucket filling" (that's what a mentor calls it). Just digging into broad topics and synthesising ideas. I don't know if these have actuated in the work yet but I imagine it's only a matter of time.
That's a great way to put it - "bucket filling." It sounds like you're in an investment phase right now, building up this broader knowledge base that will eventually feed into your compositions.
I also am pretty concerned about how AI generated music might impact streaming platform saturation.
I actually don't know. It'll certainly make the non-creative aspects less tedious. Hopefully it'll be able to help me refine my ideas and speed up my workflow.
Yes, AI tools were used mainly for propensity for mortality evaluation to narrow the target population and for data evaluation.
Machine learning was used to generate a singular propensity score, whereas traditional approaches used by the medical team was ranking based on the number of risk factors the patient had.
It was likely driven by AI hype to satisfy the company investors
It was helpful to have a singular metric to segment the population, opposed to the previous count-based ranking of potentially unequal factors.
That makes sense - having that single metric would definitely make the segmentation more straightforward and potentially more accurate than assuming all risk factors carry equal weight.
Keeping the medical team engaged in the project at a level where they felt their medical expertise was directly contributing to the project.
We back-tested on historical member data
A tool for model transparency that can be easily understood by the medical team and also allows for the operations team to monitor for model drift.
I do not believe there are any tasks that AI could help with that I prefer to do myself in my line of work.
Are you more likely to go back and forth with it throughout figuring out the pitch, or do you tend to give it all the context upfront and let it handle the task independently?

My colleagues have influenced the way I use AI because I tend to use it more often when I need to "compete" with them. If my sales for the month are low compared to them, I tend to turn to AI for help.

That sounds like a great success! What made that AI-generated strategy work so well compared to other times you've used it? Was there something different about how you approached it or the situation itself?
I've thought about it a bit but I prefer to work with AI and use it to better myself instead of competing.
